prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: side impact at intersection in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1222; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling through the intersection on a green signal when the vehicle was struck on the driver's side by Driver 2, who entered from a cross street and failed to yield. The collision was a side impact, and the damage to the struck vehicle lines up with the force and direction of the contact described by both drivers. Driver 1 reported neck pain and stiffness at the scene and was evaluated by responding medical personnel. The injury reported is consistent with the kind of forces expected in a crash of this type. A Passenger was also seated in Driver 1's vehicle at the time, and both the passenger and a bystander stated the passenger was present during the collision. Driver 2 gave a statement that generally agreed with Driver 1's account of how the crash occurred. Scene photographs were taken and are consistent with the statements obtained. Officers found no indication of prior damage to the struck vehicle. Driver 1 was confirmed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle at the time of the crash. No citations were issued at the scene pending further review.
